headline: Build one letter choice per digit
statement: Return every letter string represented by a string of telephone digits 2 through 9. Use the standard mapping 2=abc, 3=def, 4=ghi, 5=jkl, 6=mno, 7=pqrs, 8=tuv, 9=wxyz. An empty input has no combinations. Output order is unrestricted.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
intuition: Build each possible word from left to right. The first digit gives the choices for the first letter, the next digit gives the choices for the next letter, and so on. Finish a word only after choosing one allowed letter for every digit.
approach: At index i, append each letter for digits[i] to the partial word.
Recurse to i+1 and save the word only when all digits are consumed.
correctness: Each leaf has one allowed letter at every digit position. Every valid combination determines exactly one path through these choices, so all combinations appear once. Returning early for empty digits prevents the empty word being mistaken for a combination.
bruteForce: Repeatedly extend a list of all partial strings; it has the same necessary output cost but retains complete intermediate layers.

complexity.explanation: There are at most four branches per digit and each resulting word has n letters. Copied immutable prefixes held by active recursive calls use O(n^2) additional characters.

pitfalls: Do not convert the digit string to an integer; positions matter.
Handle the empty input before entering recursion.
